snapshot: The Nikkei finished the morning session at 62,930.20, up 187.63. It started weak on semiconductor profit-taking but recovered into positive territory by the break.
Prime-market breadth was 1,023 gainers, 494 decliners and 49 unchanged, showing broader internal strength than the early index action implied.
Nikkei 225 night-session futures closed at 62,510 and TOPIX futures at 3,880. Futures were at a small discount to the prior cash close.
Reuters reported soft Asian equities, Brent at $107.13, USD/JPY in the high 157s and the U.S. 10-year yield at 4.469%. Inflation and Middle East stalemate remain headwinds.
The relative-strength pocket is concentrated in easy-to-explain catalysts: Kioxia, Tokyo Enesys, ExaWizards and Muto Seiko on memory supply, earnings and shareholder returns.

drivers.why_today: Advantest and Tokyo Electron weighed on the index around 10:00, but by the midday break Kioxia and other gainers had pulled the Nikkei back into positive territory.

drivers.driver: U.S. inflation, stalled Middle East diplomacy and high oil still cap the upside
drivers.why_today: Reuters highlighted hotter U.S. inflation, the Iran stalemate and oil above $100. The index recovered, but afternoon risk appetite still depends heavily on external conditions.

drivers.driver: Stock-specific earnings, dividend and payout-policy catalysts are leading
drivers.why_today: Tokyo Enesys, Mec, Honyaku Center, ExaWizards and Muto Seiko all have clear post-close earnings or shareholder-return stories that are driving relative strength.

deep_dive.title: Kioxia: test whether NAND supply-driven relative strength can survive semiconductor profit-taking

lines: Today's Kioxia move combines AI data-center SSD demand with NAND supply-tightness speculation tied to Samsung strike risk.
The key signal is that the stock kept rising even as Tokyo Electron and Advantest weighed on the index.
Reuters reported a sharp drop in Samsung shares and labor talks failing, which strengthens the market's read-through to AI chip and memory production risk.
At the midday break, Kioxia was the largest positive contributor to the Nikkei, helping the index recover from early weakness.
Can it hold the 48,000-yen area and remain the leading semiconductor name into the afternoon.
Does real dip-buying volume remain, not just short-covering demand.
Samsung strike speculation fades and the NAND price-up narrative loses force.
Broad semiconductor profit-taking pulls the stock out of its morning high zone.
The stock has already been rising for several sessions, so if supply speculation cools, the correction can be sharp.
Hot U.S. inflation and the Middle East stalemate could reduce risk appetite for Growth and semiconductor names.
